topic.title: Finite Automata
topic.description: Study deterministic and non-deterministic finite automata. Build DFAs and NFAs, convert regular grammars, and step through input words.

config.title: Automaton Configuration
config.inputWordHelp: Each character is treated as one input symbol.

endsWith01.title: Strings ending with "01"
endsWith01.goal: Build a DFA that accepts binary strings ending with "01".
endsWith01.description: Design a DFA over {0, 1} that accepts exactly those strings whose last two symbols are "0" followed by "1" (e.g. "01", "101", "1001"). Strings ending in any other pattern must be rejected.

endsWith00.title: Strings ending with "00"
endsWith00.goal: Build a DFA that accepts binary strings ending with two zeros.
endsWith00.description: Design a DFA over {0, 1} that accepts exactly those strings whose last two symbols are both 0 (e.g. "00", "100", "1100"). Single zeros or strings ending in 1 must be rejected.

evenOnes.title: Even number of 1s
evenOnes.goal: Accept binary strings containing an even number of 1s (including zero 1s).
evenOnes.description: Design a DFA that tracks the parity of 1s seen so far. The empty string should be accepted (zero is even).

noConsecOnes.title: No two consecutive 1s
noConsecOnes.goal: Accept binary strings that never contain "11" as a substring.
noConsecOnes.description: Design a DFA that rejects any string in which two 1s appear next to each other. Strings like "0", "01", "010" are accepted; "11", "0110" are rejected.

divBy3.title: Binary numbers divisible by 3
divBy3.goal: Accept binary strings whose decimal value is divisible by 3.
divBy3.description: Build a DFA that tracks the running remainder of the binary value modulo 3. Accept the states representing remainder 0.

grammarTwoOnesZeros.title: Automaton from Grammar: 11 0ⁿ
grammarTwoOnesZeros.goal: Build a DFA for the language L = { 11 0ⁿ | n ≥ 0 }: two ones followed by any number of zeros.
grammarTwoOnesZeros.description: Construct a DFA that accepts exactly the words derived by the right-linear grammar shown below, then check whether the word "11001" belongs to the language.

grammarOnes.title: Automaton from Grammar: 1 0ⁿ 1
grammarOnes.goal: Build a DFA for the language generated by the grammar below.
grammarOnes.description: Construct a DFA that accepts exactly the words derived by this right-linear grammar. Each non-terminal becomes a state; the ε-production marks an accepting state.

grammar0011.title: Automaton from Grammar: (0011)(0011)*
grammar0011.goal: Build a DFA for the language generated by the grammar below.
grammar0011.description: Construct a DFA that accepts exactly the words derived by this right-linear grammar. Each non-terminal becomes a state; the ε-production marks an accepting state.

grammarOnesZero.title: Automaton from Grammar: 1ⁿ 0
grammarOnesZero.goal: Build a DFA for the language generated by the grammar below.
grammarOnesZero.description: Construct a DFA that accepts exactly the words derived by this right-linear grammar. Each non-terminal becomes a state; the ε-production marks an accepting state.

languageToAutomaton.title: Language → Automaton
languageToAutomaton.description: Build an automaton that accepts exactly the described set of words.

grammarToAutomaton.title: Grammar → Automaton
grammarToAutomaton.description: Every right-linear grammar defines a language. Build the DFA for the grammar shown in the exercise.

exerciseWorkspace.structuralHint: Fix the highlighted configuration issues before we can compare against the solution.
exerciseWorkspace.unbuiltBody: Add states, transitions and at least one accept state, then run Check Solution again.
exerciseWorkspace.grammarEpsilonNote: ε represents the empty word and marks an accepting (final) state.

containsAba.title: Contains substring "aba"
containsAba.description: An NFA that accepts any string over {a, b} that contains "aba" as a substring anywhere within it. Demonstrates nondeterminism.

lecture.title: One or more 0s, then a single 1 (00*1)
lecture.description: A DFA from the lecture exercise that accepts one or more '0's followed by exactly one '1' (Regex: 00*1).

endsWithAb.title: Ends with "ab"
endsWithAb.description: A DFA over {a, b} that accepts exactly the words ending in "ab" — the automaton the simulator used to start with. "aab" is accepted, "aba" is rejected.

grammar.title: Grammar → Automat
grammar.description: The right-linear grammar G = {S → 0S | 0A, A → 1A | 1} is converted into an NFA and then into a minimal DFA via subset construction. Both recognize the language L = {0ⁿ 1ᵐ | n,m ≥ 1}.

dfa.title: Deterministic Automata (DFA)
dfa.description: Follow a single run: exactly one transition per state and symbol.

nfa.title: Nondeterministic Automata (NFA)
nfa.description: Several states can be active at once — the word is accepted if any path reaches an accept state.

grammarToAutomaton.title: Grammar → Automaton
grammarToAutomaton.description: Turn a right-linear grammar into an automaton and compare the NFA with an equivalent DFA.

grammar.title: Regular Grammar → Automaton
grammar.intro: Enter a right-linear grammar. The first non-terminal on the left becomes the start symbol; non-terminals and terminals are inferred from your productions.
grammar.productionsHint: One production per line. Two formats are supported (auto-detected).
grammar.epsilonHint: To insert the empty string symbol (ε), you can either copy and paste it or type the word 'epsilon'.
grammar.grammar_epsilon_lhs_invalid: An ε production references a non-terminal that is not in the non-terminal set.
grammar.grammar_no_terminals: The grammar has no terminal symbols.
grammar.grammar_start_invalid: The start symbol is not one of the grammar's non-terminals.
grammar.grammar_lhs_invalid: A rule's left-hand side is not one of the grammar's non-terminals.
grammar.grammar_terminal_invalid: A rule uses a terminal that is not in the alphabet.
grammar.grammar_rhs_nonterminal_invalid: A rule points at a non-terminal that the grammar does not define.

errors.noProductions: No production rules found. Add at least one rule like 'S -> 0S | 1A'.
errors.missingArrow: Cannot read the production '{{line}}'. Expected the form 'LHS -> RHS'.
errors.emptyAlternative: There is an empty alternative in '{{line}}'.
errors.epsilonNotAlone: ε must stand alone as an alternative — got '{{alternative}}' in '{{line}}'.
errors.unitProduction: '{{alternative}}' in '{{line}}' is only a non-terminal. A right-linear rule needs a terminal first, for example 'aB'.
errors.undefinedNonTerminal: '{{alternative}}' in '{{line}}' is not right-linear: '{{rest}}' has no rule of its own. Write a single terminal ('A -> a') or a terminal followed by a defined non-terminal ('A -> aB').
errors.unsupportedType: Unsupported type '{{type}}'. Only 'type: grammar' is supported.
errors.structuredLine: Line {{line}}: expected 'key: value' or a production rule.
errors.structuredMissingType: The structured format requires a 'type: grammar' header.

explanation.reading: Reading symbol '{{symbol}}' at position {{pos}}. Active states: {{states}}
explanation.accepted: The word is accepted. Final states {{states}} include an accept state.
explanation.rejectedDead: The word is rejected. No reachable states (dead end).
explanation.rejected: The word is rejected. Final states {{states}} do not include an accept state.

validation.startStateMissing: Start state is not in the state set.
validation.acceptStatesInvalid: An accept state is not in the state set.
validation.transitionSourceInvalid: A transition source state is invalid.
validation.transitionTargetInvalid: A transition target state is invalid.
validation.transitionSymbolInvalid: A transition symbol is not in the alphabet.

diagram.title: State Diagram
diagram.violationEpsilon: State {{state}} has an ε-transition — not allowed in a DFA.
diagram.violationNondeterministic: State {{state}} on symbol '{{symbol}}' goes to {{targets}} — this violates DFA determinism.
